item: C1: Reflection doubling for neighbouring labels (Prop 7.1 with tuple-lift Lemma 7.2): co-location on an alpha_i facet forces A1^{-1}A2 to be the facet reflection, so an inward segment E has opposite target images with P(E'1 u E'2) = 2P(E). Alternating switch bundles on the two sheets then reach target volume e^{2rP(E)}, while the source terminals are covered by e^{rP(E)} balls.
item_type: lemma (F3 gadget: alternating two-sheet bundles; F4 flavour: exponent doubling)
provisional_grade: N3 weak candidate (novelty.json, conf 0.40 after the 2026-10-12 Peng II full-text re-check; was 0.35)
lean_status_why: Lean follows the paper's route step for step: facet agreement, then a reflection forced by the finite group, then the doubling identity, then the alternating-bundle source/target exponent comparison. It is fully proved, and good_root_neighbor_labels_eq lies on the dependency chain of all three comparator targets. The only differences are packaging (good Haar sets instead of limiting laws).
lean_gaps: Packaging of Prop 7.1. The paper states it for supports of limiting joint laws. The Lean (good_root_neighbor_labels_eq) uses explicit 'good' Haar sets whose relative mass may decay subexponentially ('No positive limiting fraction ... is required'), driven by the shrinking-enlargement diagonal diagonal_/eventually_root_neighbor_labels_eq -> exists_uniform_neighbor_label_threshold. This repackaging is at least as strong as the paper.

Invariant inner product. The paper chooses an A-invariant inner product. The Lean pulls back a Euclidean norm through a finite-orbit embedding inside the proof (FiniteLabelReflection.lean), so W keeps its own norm. The idea is the same.

Doubling identity. The paper cites translation invariance and segment homogeneity of P. The Lean derives P(seg w u seg -w) = 2 segmentSupport w from SupportDatum.balanced (unimodularity) via basisSupport_neg, i.e. p(-w) = p(w). The identity is therefore an elementary 13-line consequence of unimodular balance.
Lemma 7.2 (tuple lifts) is split across tuple_lift_projection_volume, exists_increment_volume_of_separated_tuples and exists_sequence_path_tuple_lifts.

The cluster lemmas take Prop-valued inputs as hypotheses (RemezPolynomialInput, ExponentialLinearRealizationInput, Nilpotent{Dynkin,ExponentialHaar}Input). These are proved elsewhere (remezPolynomialInput in RemezFromInterpolation.lean; exponentialLinearRealizationInput_intrinsic), and the comparator targets carry no Input hypotheses.

Comparator main_uniform_bounded_height asks only for 'some finite subgroup A'. This is weaker than the paper's explicit A_G, but the proof instantiates templateSymmetryGroup, and C1 is used with that group. Not a gap for C1.

Size profile. The finite-dimensional reflection + doubling step is tiny (affine_labels_eq_of_template_comparison dominates 13 decls / 298 lines; exists_reflected_direction_of_finite_labels 4 / 98; templateSupport_opposite_segments 3 / 30). The cluster good_root_neighbor_labels_eq dominates 287 decls / 7,128 lines in 121 files, 264 of them via good_affine_templates_support_le (coupled-profile alternating volume comparison; path_alternating_product_exponent_le alone 80 decls / 2,163 lines). The non-classical content is the alternating cross-sheet bundle comparison, not the reflection lemma.
Text-level check only. Not built (shared checkout); Lean trusted as published.

comparator.note: group_recognition -> group_recognition_of_gromov -> recognition_and_lattice_of_gromov -> exists_uniform_height_intrinsic joins the chain below; lattice_recognition goes through group_recognition. BFS over the `uses` graph of data/items/255_lean.json, with call sites checked in source (good_root_neighbor_labels_eq applies affine_labels_eq_of_template_comparison and good_affine_templates_support_le).

lean_source.name: OAI.PolycyclicRecognition.SupportDatum
lean_source.text:
/-- The finite algebraic data of the segment-support formula. -/
structure SupportDatum (W I B : Type*) [AddCommGroup W] [Module ℝ W]
    [Fintype I] [Fintype B] where
  weight : I → W →ₗ[ℝ] ℝ
  multiplicity : B → I → ℕ
  positive : ∀ b i, 0 < multiplicity b i
  balanced : ∀ b w, ∑ i, (multiplicity b i : ℝ) * weight i w = 0
  separates : ∀ w, (∀ i, weight i w = 0) → w = 0

lean_source.name: OAI.PolycyclicRecognition.SupportDatum.basisSupport / segmentSupport
lean_source.text:
/-- The support exponent contributed by one bracket-word basis. -/
noncomputable def basisSupport (b : B) (w : W) : ℝ :=
  ∑ i, (D.multiplicity b i : ℝ) * max 0 (D.weight i w)

/-- The support exponent of the segment from zero to `w`. -/
noncomputable def segmentSupport (w : W) : ℝ :=
  Finset.univ.sup' Finset.univ_nonempty (fun b => D.basisSupport b w)

lean_source.text:
/-- The group in equation (support-symmetry-group) of `boxes.tex`. -/
def templateSymmetryGroup (D : SupportDatum W I B) : Subgroup (W ≃ₗ[ℝ] W) where
  carrier := {A | ∀ E : Set W, IsCompact E → E.Nonempty → Convex ℝ E →
    D.templateSupport (A '' E) = D.templateSupport E}

/-- Opposite images have twice the single-segment volume exponent. -/
theorem reflected_segment_support
    (A C : PolycyclicRecognition.templateSymmetryGroup D) {w : W}
    (hw : w ≠ 0) (hreflect : C.val w = -A.val w) :
    D.templateSupport (A.val '' segment ℝ 0 w) = D.segmentSupport w ∧
    D.templateSupport (C.val '' segment ℝ 0 w) = D.segmentSupport w ∧
    D.templateSupport ((A.val '' segment ℝ 0 w) ∪ (C.val '' segment ℝ 0 w)) =
      2 * D.segmentSupport w ∧ 0 < D.segmentSupport w := by ...

theorem exists_reflection_templates
    (D : SupportDatum W I B) (A C : templateSymmetryGroup D) (hne : A ≠ C)
    (ℓ : W →ₗ[ℝ] ℝ) (hℓ : ℓ ≠ 0) (b₁ b₂ p : W)
    (α : J → W →ₗ[ℝ] ℝ) (c : J → ℝ) (hp : ∀ j, α j p ≤ c j)
    (hactive : ∀ j, α j p = c j → ∃ t : ℝ, 0 < t ∧ α j = t • ℓ)
    {ρ : ℝ} (hρ : 0 < ρ)
    (hagree : ∀ q, ℓ q = ℓ p → ‖q - p‖ < ρ → A.val q + b₁ = C.val q + b₂) :
    ∃ w : W, ℓ w < 0 ∧ C.val w = -A.val w ∧
      ((fun x => x + p) '' segment ℝ 0 w) ⊆ {x | ∀ j, α j x ≤ c j} ∧

      let E₂ := C.val '' segment ℝ 0 w
      0 < D.templateSupport E ∧ D.templateSupport E₁ = D.templateSupport E ∧
        D.templateSupport E₂ = D.templateSupport E ∧
        D.templateSupport (E₁ ∪ E₂) = 2 * D.templateSupport E := by ...

speedup_targets.title: EFW: height-respecting QIs and QI rigidity of Diestel-Leader graphs DL(n,n) / lamplighters F wr Z
speedup_targets.statement: Every (K,C)-quasi-isometry of DL(m,n) is at bounded distance B(K,C) from a height-respecting map (height-preserving, or height-reversing when m=n); hence F wr Z and F' wr Z are QI iff |F|,|F'| are powers of a common integer.
speedup_targets.reference: Eskin-Fisher-Whyte, Coarse differentiation of quasi-isometries I (Annals 176, 2012) and II: Rigidity for Sol and lamplighter groups (Annals 177, 2013), arXiv math/0511647, 0706.0940
speedup_targets.current_proof_size: about 40 + 42 journal pages for I+II (the orientation-consistency sub-step is a few pages); no Lean formalization anywhere known
speedup_targets.how_item_helps: For m=n the only nontrivial label is the flip A=-1, i.e. the reflection at the endpoint facet of the height interval. If adjacent tiles of the coarse-differentiation tiling carried opposite labels, C1's alternating bundles (one step on each sheet, tree box volumes exact powers of n) give a target terminal count n^{2r|E|} against a source count n^{r|E|}. This would replace EFW's orientation-consistency step. It does NOT replace coarse differentiation or the quadrilateral argument that makes each tile height-respecting, which is the bulk of EFW.

lean_feasibility.score: statable with < 300 lines of new definitions
lean_feasibility.statable_with: SimpleGraph + SimpleGraph.dist (Mathlib); OAI MetricQuasiEquivalence / SelfQuasiIsometry for the QI notion; OAI SupportDatum instance W=R, weights +-log n (balanced) for the finite-dimensional half
lean_feasibility.missing: regular tree with a chosen end and Busemann height (~80-120 lines), horocyclic product DL(m,n) as a graph with height map (~60-100 lines), height-respecting predicate (~20 lines); the proof would need a tree box calculus (major)

speedup_targets.title: Ferragut: QIs of horospherical products are close to product maps (swap-consistency when factors are isomorphic)
speedup_targets.statement: For horospherical products X bowtie Y of proper geodesic Gromov-hyperbolic (e.g. Heintze) spaces, every QI is at bounded distance from a product map, composed with the factor swap when X is isometric to Y.
speedup_targets.reference: T. Ferragut, Geometric rigidity of quasi-isometries in horospherical products, Algebr. Geom. Topol. 26:3 (2026) 863-954, arXiv 2211.04093
speedup_targets.how_item_helps: Only for unimodular products with isomorphic factors (the swap is the flip label), where the device could replace the cross-region swap-consistency step. Ferragut's core tool, height-respecting tetrahedric quadrilaterals (Sec. 2.3), is a different mechanism and is what makes each region standard. Non-unimodular products have no swap, so the device is vacuous there.

open_problems.title: Two-group bounded height: QIs between distinct unimodular real-triangulable groups
open_problems.statement: If G, G' are connected simply connected real-triangulable unimodular Lie groups and F : G -> G' is a (K,C)-QI, then there is a linear L : W -> W' with P_{G'} o L = P_G (so p' o L = p and L conjugates A_G to A_{G'}) and ||pi'F(g) - pi'F(1) - L pi(g)|| <= B(G,G',K,C).
open_problems.reference: Not claimed in 255 (Thm 1.4 is for self-QIs only). It is a step toward Cornulier's Conjecture 19.113 (QI completely solvable groups are isomorphic; Cornulier 2018, 'On the quasi-isometric classification of locally compact groups'), restricted to the unimodular case. Peng I treats QIs between two groups of her class locally (search snippet, arXiv 0802.2596).
open_problems.status: open in this generality as far as found (unverified); known for Sol(a,b) (EFW) and, locally, for nondegenerate split abelian-by-abelian groups (Peng)
open_problems.obstruction_match: Identical to C1's. Neighbouring sheets carry labels L1, L2 : W -> W' with P' o Li = P, so L1^{-1}L2 lies in A_G; agreement on a facet forces a reflection, and the doubling identity holds on the source side.
open_problems.adaptation_sketch: Generalize affine_labels_eq_of_template_comparison to two SupportData (about 50-100 lines; transport through L1). The heavy work is making the rest of the height engine two-group, with the source box calculus on G and the target box calculus on G'. Prop 9.4 and Sec. 10 are written for a single group.
open_problems.payoff: high: a new QI invariant, the polyhedral norm (W,p) up to linear isometry, for all unimodular solvable Lie groups. It would distinguish many pairs that Dehn functions and cone dimension cannot.
open_problems.how_item_helps: Supplies the label-agreement step verbatim. That counts as device reuse in a theorem that is not a corollary of Thm 1.4, though the proof shape stays close to 255's.

open_problems.statement: For a non-unimodular real-triangulable G (e.g. R^2 acting on R^3 by weights alpha1, alpha2, alpha3 with alpha1+alpha2+alpha3 != 0, where a reflection swaps alpha1 and alpha2), every self-QI satisfies the bounded-height conclusion of Thm 1.4 for a finite label group.

open_problems.obstruction_match: Mismatched neighbour labels that differ by a reflection fixing a facet.
open_problems.adaptation_sketch: The `balanced` field of SupportDatum fails, so P(E'1 u E'2) = 2P(E) is false. Instead use P(E' u RE') = P(E) + sum over the swapped weights of the extra positive part, which is strictly larger than P(E) whenever R exchanges weights of opposite sign on E'. The source packing bound and Haar-preserving weight dilations also need repair, because 255 uses unimodularity there.
open_problems.how_item_helps: The mechanism (alternating bundles realize the union exponent) carries over. The exact doubling identity does not.

open_problems.title: QI rigidity of Diestel-Leader graphs DL_d(q), d >= 3, and higher-rank lamplighter groups
open_problems.statement: Every QI of the horocyclic product of d >= 3 trees DL_d(q) is at bounded distance from a height-respecting map, composed with a permutation of the trees. Consequently f.g. groups QI to higher-rank lamplighters are classified.
open_problems.reference: Bartholdi-Neuhauser-Woess, Horocyclic products of trees, JEMS 2008 (arXiv math/0601417): open questions on QI classification of DL graphs; Dymarz-Peng-Taback, NYJM 21 (2015) (higher-rank lamplighters)
open_problems.status: open as far as found (searches found only d=2: EFW; two-factor horospherical products: Ferragut). Unverified.
open_problems.obstruction_match: Strong. The height space W = {x in R^d : sum x = 0} with weights x_i is balanced (unimodular-like). The label group is S_d acting by permutations, and its transpositions are reflections whose fixed hyperplanes are facets of the box polytope. Labels on sheets one step apart in a tree direction can differ exactly by such a transposition.
open_problems.adaptation_sketch: Port the support calculus to trees, where box volumes are exact powers of q and no Remez or Lie machinery is needed. A higher-rank coarse differentiation for products of trees is also needed (the Peng-style step), and that is the main cost. C1 then rules out transposition mismatches between neighbouring tiles.
open_problems.payoff: high (BNW questions; a totally disconnected analogue of Peng/Sol_5)
open_problems.how_item_helps: Device reuse in a setting outside 255's theorem: the groups are not polycyclic and not lattices in Lie groups.

negative_controls.title: Real hyperbolic plane H^2 = Aff+(R) (non-unimodular Heintze group), and H^2 x H^2
negative_controls.expected: device fails; Thm-1.4 analogue is FALSE
negative_controls.why: An elliptic isometry of H^2 moves the Busemann height unboundedly, so no bounded-height theorem holds (proved-false analogue). In Lean the SupportDatum field `balanced` cannot be instantiated: one weight alpha > 0 with sum m*alpha != 0. So basisSupport_neg, and with it templateSupport_opposite_segments (P([-w,w]) = 2P([0,w])), is unavailable; here P([-w,w]) = P([0,w]). Any 'reuse' claimed in a non-unimodular rank-one setting is spurious.

negative_controls.title: Groups with trivial label group: BS(1,n), Sol(a,b) with a != b, Heintze groups R semidirect R^n
negative_controls.why: A_G = {1}, so 'neighbouring labels agree' holds trivially. Height control there comes from other mechanisms (Farb-Mosher tree projection, EFW, boundary quasiconformal theory).

negative_controls.title: Nilpotent/abelian groups (W = 0) and global flips
negative_controls.expected: device vacuous; must not exclude the Sol flip
negative_controls.why: P is identically 0 and there are no labels; in Euclidean geometry, sheets one step apart are at bounded distance, so continuity alone forces agreement. Also, a global reflection label (Sol's (x,y,t) -> (y,x,-t)) is an isometry. The device only rules out MISMATCHED neighbours, so a proposed reuse that proves global orientation preservation is wrong.

top5.argument: This is the cleanest device reuse outside 255's own theorem: Thm 1.4 is for self-QIs and gives nothing for F : G -> G'. The labelled-sheet configuration is identical, and the finite-dimensional half (affine_labels_eq_of_template_comparison, 13 decls / 298 lines) generalizes to two SupportData almost verbatim. Every ingredient of the statement already exists in the OAI library (SimplyConnectedSolvableLieModel, HeightSpace, MetricQuasiEquivalence, ModelIsUnimodular). The payoff is a new QI invariant, (W,p) up to linear isometry. Caveat: the reuse is 'same proof, two groups'. It shows the device transports, but it is weak evidence of an independent speedup.

Here the device must genuinely adapt. Without unimodularity the doubling identity is false; it would be replaced by a strict union-exponent gain whenever the reflection swaps weights of opposite sign. The statement is main_uniform_bounded_height minus `huni`. This is the best test of whether the mechanism (alternating bundles realize a union exponent) or merely the identity (balance) carries the weight. Confidence is low because non-unimodular packing also breaks.

This is the strongest out-of-class match. DL_d(q) has a balanced height space, label group S_d, and transpositions as facet reflections, and tree boxes have exact volumes, so C1's volume half becomes elementary. It is open per BNW and outside 255 (not polycyclic). The cost is a higher-rank coarse differentiation for products of trees, which C1 does not supply.

This is the only KNOWN out-of-class theorem where C1 competes with an existing proof: the orientation consistency for DL(n,n) in EFW II. It can be measured (proof length of the consistency step with and without C1), but the expected speedup is low because coarse differentiation and quadrilaterals dominate EFW.

Mixed real/p-adic Sol lattices such as Z[1/p]^2 semidirect Z have a balanced height space with a flip, so C1 applies once a mixed support calculus exists. The status is unverified and confidence is low, but the statement is cheap to write with Mathlib's Padic and SemidirectProduct.

peng_II_sec4_comparison: READ IN FULL 2026-10-12 (arXiv:1002.4451v1, pp. 17-31). Same sub-problem as C1, different mechanism. Thm 4.1 (root-class horocycles go near horocycles over the whole big box) is proved EFW II-style: S, S-hat and H graphs of shadow vertices, Gromov products in the hyperbolic slice W_l^- x| R v_l, the illegal-circuit loop Lemma 4.2.5, a rank-1 geodesic counting Lemma 4.3.2 used only to force divergence, Props 4.3.1-4.3.2 and Thm 4.2 ('the loop that prevents blocking'). Cor 4.0.1 then equalises linear parts by a measure-vs-length argument (equal-measure horocycle pieces at different heights; connecting geodesics of length O(diam B) would need preimages of length e^{eps diam B}). Rank 1 'follows exactly the same proof as in [EFW2]'; higher rank 'basically consists of many rank 1 argument'. So the earlier guess that rank >= 2 uses a separate mechanism is corrected: it is the same EFW II rank-1 topology repeated. No facet reflection, no exponent doubling, no alternating two-sheet bundles: C1 is not a close variant of Peng. Uniformity point stands: C1 treats rank 1 and rank >= 2 by one volume count, Peng by repeated quadrilateral/loop arguments.
